question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To make both ends meet

options.text: To take back what you have said

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To make both ends meet"** means:

 
 
• To live within one’s income. (अपनी आय के भीतर रहकर जीवन जीना)
 
 
 
• **Example:** Despite the rising prices, she managed **to make both ends meet by cutting down on unnecessary expenses.**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To take back what you have said** (जो आपने कहा उसे वापस लेना):

 
 
• **Example:** He had to take back what he said after realizing it was incorrect.
 
 
 
• **To anticipate** (पूर्वानुमान करना):
 
 
• **Example:** She could anticipate the outcome of the meeting based on the preliminary discussions.
 
 
 
• **Quite worthless** (पूरी तरह से बेकार):
 
 
• **Example:** The broken watch was quite worthless and couldn't be repaired.
